newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL key stocks index ends off low, down 1.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: KL key stocks index ends off low, down 1.4 pct.

text.p: Malaysian blue chip stocks bounced back to end down 1.36 percent, or 15.73 points, at 1,136.78.
It had hit a low of 1,113.47 earlier in the afternoon.
Sentiment was battered by confusion over Bank Negara's plans to curb lending to the property market and for share purchase financing.
Sime Darby was the day's most active stock, closing 30 cents higher at 8.50 after being five cents down in afternoon trade.
Shares were also dragged down by brokerage houses making cash calls on their customers after share prices dropped around seven percent over the week, dealer and analysts said.
"The selling was somewhat of an over reaction, they were really bashed down," said Lynn Cheah Lee Ling, assistant manager of fund managers BHLB Asset Management in Kuala Lumpur.
Blue chip shares had dropped as much as 3.4 percent, before bouncing back on a technical rebound as U.K. funds selectively bought blue-chip stocks after 1530 local (0730 GMT), she said.
Analysts said local funds also entered the market in the afternoon as buyers of blue chips, adding to the rebound.
Market volume surged to 459 million shares, valued at 2,763.48 million ringgit. Losers thumped gainers 555 to 130.
Bank Negara had said in its 1996 annual report published last Friday, that it planned to restrict banks from lending more than 20 percent of their total outstanding loans for property purchases.

Sime Darby had fallen as analysts said the company's earnings would be affected due to its significant exposure to the property and finance sectors. But local funds support for the stock saw it ending in positive territory, dealers said.

"Among the index-linked stocks it is one of the easiest to push up because it is one of the cheapest, and it has a large-weighting on the Composite Index," said a dealer at a local bank-backed brokerage house.
Other blue chips were not so lucky. Malayan Banking closed 25 cents down at 27 ringgit, even though it rebounded from an intraday low of 26.75.
"There was a lot of local support for Maybank at 27 ringgit," said the dealer.
"A lot of next week's performance depends on what happens tonight in the U.S. especially with non-farm payrolls and jobless data coming out," said the dealer.
"The long-term view for the Malaysian market is still positive, but in the short term we are negative," said Fiona Leong, head of research at J.M. Sassoon in Kuala Lumpur.
"My advice for next week would be to stay away from property stocks. They affect everything on the market from construction to plantations and banking stocks," said Cheah.
According to the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange, Friday's intraday plunge of 39.04 points was the largest point drop since March 21, 1994, when the key index fell 52.88 points.
